questions.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
questions.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4-3}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
questions.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6-(-2)}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$

questions.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
v={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we calculate the inverse of $T$:

$$
{T}^{-1}=\frac{1}{(5)(1)-(6)(2)}[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}].

$$
v=-\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{7} \\ \frac{4}{7}\end{aligned}].

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(3,2),(7,5),$ and $(2,2).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(-2,2)$
- $(1,1)$
- $(0,0)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{9-8}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(1,0),(1,1),(-2,2).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(-1,0),(1,0),$ and $(0,1).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(1,0)$
- $(-1,0)$
- $(0,2)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-2-0}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(1,0),(-1,0),(0,\frac{1}{2}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

The parallelogram $P$ is mapped to the parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ has vertices $(2,-5),(3,-6),(4,-8),$ and $(3,-7).$ Which of the following are vertices of $P?$

- $(1,3)$
- $(3,3)$
- $(2,3)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${P}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $P$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{0-1}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $P$ are $(1,2),(3,3),(4,4),(2,3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The quadrilateral $Q$ is mapped to the quadrilateral ${Q}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The quadrilateral ${Q}^{′}$ has vertices $(0,4),(-4,4),(12,4),$ and $(7,3).$ Which of the following are vertices of $Q?$

- $(-2,4)$
- $(1,-2)$
- $(4,4)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${Q}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $Q$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2-0}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 & 8 & 4 \\ 8 & 8 & 8 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 4 & 2 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(-2,4),(-4,4),(4,4),(2,3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(3,4),(0,2),$ and $(7,10).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(0,1)$
- $(2,3)$
- $(1,0)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4-2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(1,1),(-1,2),(2,3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
